messages.subject: All intercepts are 0 except one? Possible recoding problem
parts:
Hi! 

I've encountered some weird behavior and haven't been able to straighten out what's going on. 

This is a sample of the output of summary(fit1,fit.measures=TRUE, standardized=TRUE)

Intercepts: Estimate  Std.Err  z-value  P(>|z|)   Std.lv  Std.all
.item1         0.000                               0.000    0.000
.item2         0.000                               0.000    0.000
.item3         0.000                               0.000    0.000
.item4         0.000                               0.000    0.000
.item5         0.000                               0.000    0.000
.item6         0.000                               0.000    0.000
.item7         1.170    0.004  298.045   0.000    1.170    3.116
.item8         0.000                               0.000    0.000


Item 7 is a variable I attempted to recode. 

When solving a different issue, I stumbled across a readout that indicates that lavaan believes this variable has the number of levels it had before recoding, not after. (This is a table that returns after a cfa fails due to items with no variance. It has the following column names: "name idx nobs type exo user mean var nlev  lnam"). The nlev and lnam values for item 7 reflect the number of levels and "names" before the recode. I don't know, but I assume this is the cause of the anomaly in the "intercepts" readout, because the only difference between item7 and the other items is that i recoded it. 

I have tried to put in some recoded some binary variables as well (hoping that 0,1 instead of 1, NA is the solution to "no variance") and lavaan reports their old number of levels as well.

I have inspected each, and the recoding was successful-- the nlev and lnam values should be different. However, levels() of any item returns NULL, because of their data types, so I can't directly change the levels or names. 

Does anyone know what I've done wrong, or how I can fix this? 

Thanks, 
Karen 



--

parts:
I'm afraid it's quite a large model and there are a ton of variables (i.e demographics) in the df that are necessary for other tests, but aren't used in this model. I'll try to pull out what I think is important, but feel free to ask for more. 

First, I stored each of the columns into a variable: 
i.e. 

item1 <- data$item1
item2 <- data$item2

these are all likert style items with, for example, responses of 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 or NA. Some are smaller (ie. 1, 2, 3 or NA). 

there are a couple binary ones, too, which I stored in this way: 
item3<- data$item3
item3[is.na(item3)] <- 0 

I did this because if all the responses are 1 or NA, there's no variance and the model will not run. (I can't confirm that this works, because lavaan doesn't recognize the new level. Therefore I have yet to run the model successfully with these binary variables in it.)

For the anomalous variable described in my initial question, I recoded the variable in order to collapse categories 2 and 3 ("no" and "i don't know")  
 
item7 <- data$item7
item7[item7 == 3] <- 2 
item7[item7 == 2] <- 0

Then, I created a model, i.e: 

CModel <- 
'  LV1 =~ item1 + item2 +item3 + item 4
LV2 =~ item5 + item6 + item7
LV3 =~ item8 + item9
LV4=~ item10 + item11 +item12

LV2~ LV3
LV1 ~ LV3
LV4 ~ LV1 + LV2'

(The above mimics the exact structure of the model, but does not include all the items. There are a lot). 

Then I fit the model using CFA,

fit1 <- cfa(CModel1, data = data, meanstructure = TRUE,
           ordered =c(item1, item2, item4, item5, item6, item7. .. )

When I try to included the binary variables in the model and in ordered(), it fails. If I include the binary variables in the model, but exclude them from ordered(), that at least allows the model to run, but the binary variables are not included in the summary report and the output looks the same as if they were not included in the model.  

I have tried including item7 in ordered() and excluding it.  When it is included, I get this error: 
Error in lav_samplestats_step1(Y = Data, ov.names = ov.names, ov.types = ov.types,  : 
  lavaan ERROR: some categories of variable `CAppHasPolicy' are empty in group 1; frequencies are [181 37 0]  

If I keep it excluded, the model converges with the following warning : 

Warning message:
In muthen1984(Data = X[[g]], ov.names = ov.names[[g]], ov.types = ov.types,  :
  lavaan WARNING: trouble constructing W matrix; used generalized inverse for A11 submatrix

I can still get a summary of the model: 

summary(fit1,fit.measures=TRUE, standardized=TRUE)

The summary has the problem in the original email, quoted here:
